rule: Flash on a protection/reactive card means it can respond to threats at instant speed — tag as 'reactive-protection', not the generic 'flash-instant-speed'
Cards that say 'This creature is the chosen type in addition to its other types' must include 'can-become-chosen-type' in synergy_tags. This is critical for tribal decks.
pattern: this creature is the chosen type in addition

rule: Replacement effects that add extra counters ('that many plus one', 'twice that many') are passive-permanent by definition — always tag as 'passive-permanent' AND 'replacement-effect'
Do not use overly broad tags like 'tribal-synergy' — instead be specific: 'human-tribal', 'elf-tribal', etc. Generic 'tribal-synergy' is too vague to be useful for graph edges.

A card that puts counters on ALL creatures you control (board-wide) must be tagged 'board-wide-counter-placer'. A card that puts counters on a single target is 'single-target-counter-placer'. This distinction is critical for synergy matching.
Sol Ring must always have role='ramp' and include 'staple-mana-rock' and 'colorless-ramp' in synergy_tags. It is the most universal ramp piece in EDH.
correct: role=ramp, synergy_tags includes staple-mana-rock and colorless-ramp

rule: Cards that untap creatures or permanents (including the {Q} untap symbol, 'untap target creature', or granting untap abilities) MUST include 'untap' in provides. This is critical for combo detection — untap effects enable infinite loops with tap abilities like Krenko.

NEVER use 'creature-board' as a wants tag — it matches 38% of all cards and is too generic to form useful graph edges. Instead use SPECIFIC sub-tags: 'sacrifice-fodder' (wants disposable creatures to sacrifice), 'creature-count-matters' (scales with number of creatures), 'creature-power-matters' (cares about power/toughness), 'equip-target' (needs a creature to attach to), 'combat-attackers' (needs creatures to attack with), 'tap-ability-creatures' (needs creatures that tap for value).
correct: sacrifice-fodder / creature-count-matters / creature-power-matters / equip-target / combat-attackers / tap-ability-creatures

rule: Cards with Toxic or Infect MUST include 'poison-counter-placement' in provides. Cards with Proliferate MUST include 'proliferate' in provides. These tags connect poison/infect cards to proliferate synergies.

Cards whose oracle text explicitly references a creature type (e.g., 'Other Humans you control get +1/+1' or 'Whenever a Goblin enters') MUST include 'X-tribal' in provides, where X is the creature type. Being a creature of type X alone does NOT qualify — the oracle text must reference the type.

Cards that tax opponents (make spells cost more, force payment on actions) MUST include 'stax-tax' in provides. Cards that deny resources (tap permanents, prevent untapping, destroy lands) MUST include 'resource-denial' or 'mana-denial' in provides.

Do NOT use generic 'combat-events' as a wants tag for every creature — it matches 23% of cards. Only use it for cards that specifically trigger on combat damage or have combat-specific abilities. A vanilla creature that attacks does NOT want 'combat-events'.
correct: combat-attackers (if card specifically cares about attacking)
example_card: Swords to Plowshares does NOT want combat-events
